text:
Jess (support): Hey folks, customer report: intermittent 5xxs from hosted API v1 (/v1/generate). They expect 429 but are seeing 502/503s. Happening since ~08:10 UTC. Correlation ids attached. :warning:
Ryan (oncall): Thanks Jess, can you paste a couple of example request IDs and timestamps?
Jess (support): request ids: req_8c9f2a, req_b3d11f, timestamps 2026-03-17T08:11:04Z, 08:12:37Z. Payloads are short. Customer says spike started after a deploy at 08:00 UTC.
Samir (infra): grabbing logs now. Quick thought: quota/rate-limiter should return 429 for token quota hits, not 5xx. Could be a misroute to an older quota-orch that has a blocking dependency. :eyes:
Maria (sre): I'm seeing the same request IDs in the gateway logs. Upstream to quota-orch returns a 504 on some calls, and gateway translates to 502. Here's an example trace: 
```
gateway_id=gw-1 trace=req_8c9f2a
-> route: /quota/check -> upstream: quota-orch-v2 internal:10.2.12.8:8080
upstream_status=504 duration_ms=12051 dependency=auth-cache
```
Ryan (oncall): auth-cache dependency timing out at ~12s. Default quota timeout is 10s, so we're hitting edge. Why did it go to quota-orch-v2? We recently changed routing in the last deploy.
Samir (infra): Confirmed: deploy changed service selector label for token-quota -> service alias "quota-orch" now points to v2 behind a new sidecar. v2 has a flaky redis connection to auth-cache. When auth-cache times out, quota-orch returns 500/504 instead of returning a 429 when limits exceeded.
Jess (support): Customer impact: some requests that should have been rate-limited are failing for upstream 5xx. They're seeing errors in product and escalating.
Maria (sre): Immediate mitigations: 1) Roll traffic back to quota-orch-v1 (older stable) or 2) increase gateway upstream timeout + add 5xx->429 mapping for quota endpoints while we fix v2. Which is faster?
Samir (infra): Rollback is fastest. I'll open a rollback PR and start a canary rollback to v1 for traffic to quota-orch. If rollback is risky, we can flip the service alias back.
Ryan (oncall): Also push a short-term rule in the gateway to coerce 5xx from quota-orch endpoints to 429 for requests that match token-quota routes. Patch: 
```
# nginx/gateway snippet (temp)
location /quota/check {
  proxy_pass http://quota-orch;
  proxy_next_upstream error timeout http_502 http_503 http_504;
  # if upstream returns 5xx and request contains X-Quota-Check, map to 429
}
```
(we'll implement as header-based response rewrite in gateway config).
Jess (support): Customer notified that we're investigating and offered to throttle them client-side. They've accepted temporary mitigation.
Maria (sre): Repro steps for infra: 
1) curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"input":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate
2) Run a proxy that injects auth-cache latency (e.g., tc qdisc) to simulate 12s dependency timeout.
Expected: gateway should return 429 when quota exceeded. Observed: 5xx/502 when auth-cache times out.

Samir (infra): Root cause summary: recent deploy changed service alias -> routed quota checks to v2 which calls auth-cache synchronously; when auth-cache times out, v2 returns 5xx instead of handling locally. Action items: 
- Rollback alias to quota-orch-v1 (PR #4289) (in progress)
- Patch quota-orch-v2 to 1) fail-open for quota checks for fallback to in-memory counters, 2) ensure proper 4xx for client quota hits (ticket INF-321)
- Add gateway rule to map quota endpoint 5xx->429 for a short window (hotfix GW-110)
- Add e2e test for quota->auth-cache failure mode

Ryan (oncall): I'm running the rollback now, will update timeline. ETA ~6m. :hammer_and_wrench:
Jess (support): Notifying customer with ETA. Thanks. :pray:
Samir (infra): Rollback started, traffic shifting. Monitoring metrics: error rate for /v1/generate dropping in canary.
Maria (sre): Keep an eye on latency and 429 rates. Once stable, we'll close this thread and follow up with postmortem.
SupportBot: Incident labelled P2 and alert created: INC-20260317-08. Logged by Jess (support).
